# 🧱 SPIKE beginner examples: Sharpshooter ESP32CAM Vision Sensor (school edition)

[🔙 Back to the Sharpshooter product page](/en/sensors/esp32cam/index.md) | Have the **WRO edition (HUE12)**? See the [WRO edition beginner examples](/en/sensors/esp32cam/spike-examples-wro.md)

> [!NOTE]
> The Pybricks programs below are the same files as on the Chinese page, so the **comments inside the code are in Chinese**. The English explanation under each example tells you what every line does.

This page is written for people who have **never written a program before**. The 5 examples start with "seeing a color as a number" and build up step by step to "the robot turns its head to face a color blob" and "sound an alarm when someone walks by". Every example comes in 3 versions; just pick the one you have:

| Version | Who it's for | How to open the example file |
|---|---|---|
| 🟨 **The official LEGO SPIKE App** (blocks) | Schools, first-time SPIKE users | Download the `.llsp3` → open the SPIKE App → top-left "File" → "Open" → pick the file |
| 🟦 **The MBC Blocks website** (Chinese blocks) | People who want Chinese blocks or need more sensor data | Open the [MBC SPIKE Blocks website](https://mbc-spike-blocks.mbcrobot.workers.dev) → top menu "File → Open" (or press Ctrl+O) → pick the downloaded `.abp` |
| 🐍 **Pybricks** (Python text code) | People who want to learn typed programming | Open [code.pybricks.com](https://code.pybricks.com) → "Import a file" in the file panel on the left → import **both** the example file and `MBC_cam_school_Lib.py` → open the example → press ▶ to run |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - **The MBC Blocks website and Pybricks need the hub flashed with the Pybricks firmware first** (on the MBC Blocks website, the top menu "SPIKE Hub → Install/Update Pybricks firmware" does it, about 3 minutes; you can switch back to the original LEGO firmware with the SPIKE App any time). The official LEGO App needs no change.
> - The official LEGO App used here is the **Education edition (SPIKE 3)**. In the home edition (Robot Inventor), "color" only goes **0 to 10** (one tenth of the Education edition), so you have to change the numbers in example 2 yourself.
> - The numbers on this page are for the **firmware currently shipping** (hue 0 to 100). How to check: after power-up, look at the `X` number at the top of the sensor screen. If it **tops out around 98**, you have the new version; if it goes above 100 (up to 159), it is the old firmware; please contact us for an update first.

> [!NOTE]
> **Example 6** at the end is an advanced bonus, **Pybricks only**: the value it uses lives in a new mode of the sensor firmware from 2026-10 onward, which the blocks in the official LEGO App and the MBC Blocks website cannot read.

## Before you start: set the color to look for on the sensor

The Sharpshooter has to be "told" which color to look for first, and that is **only done with the buttons on the sensor body** (a program cannot change it). The setting is saved in the sensor and survives a reboot.

**Do these 3 things first**
1. **Plug the sensor into the hub and turn the hub on.** If the sensor screen stays on "LEGO Sync… / connect…", it is waiting for the hub; the picture only appears after the hub is on (you cannot set it up without a hub).
2. **Put the colored brick you want to use in front of the lens first.** The picture **freezes** when you enter setup, so place the brick before you press.
3. Buttons: the body has three buttons, **Left, OK (middle), Right**, plus one **side button**. Short-press the side button = enter the menu / go back one level.

**Setup 1: COLOR (see a color, gives "hue", for examples 1 and 2)**
1. When the top of the screen shows `RUN`, **short-press the side button** → `SET 1:COLOR` appears at the top.
2. Press **OK** → `SET X`: the picture freezes; use **Left/Right** to move the red vertical line onto the brick.
3. Press **OK** → `SET Y`: use **Left/Right** to move the green horizontal line onto the brick.
4. Press **OK** → `TOL_HUE` (color tolerance, keep the default 15 for now) → press **OK** → `TOL_STA` (keep the default) → press **OK** again to save and return to `RUN`.

**Setup 2: TRACK (track a blob, gives "blob X/Y/area", for examples 3 and 4)**
1. On the `RUN` screen, **short-press the side button** → press **Right** to switch to `SET 2:TRACK` → press **OK**.
2. `SET X`, `SET Y`: the center of the crosshair must be **right on the middle of the blob** (it only samples the color at that one center point).
3. `TOL_HUE`, `TOL_STA`: everything on screen with the same color as the target gets marked; adjust until **only your brick is marked**.
4. `MIN AREA` (smallest blob): if small specks in the background get boxed, raise it a little → press **OK** to save; a tracking box appears on screen.

> [!WARNING]
> **The picture is upside down after changing a camera setting. What now?** The current firmware has a known issue: changing anything in `SET MODE CAM` (the camera menu), including turning on the fill light `Flash LED`, **flips the picture upside down**, and the blob Y flips with it. The fix: in the same camera menu, switch **`V-Flip` to ON**; the picture is upright again and the setting is remembered.

**Should I turn on the fill light?** **Not yet.** The ESP32-CAM fill light is very bright; LEGO brick surfaces reflect it and turn white, so the color gets harder to recognize, not easier. Only turn it on when the field is really dark (and check the V-Flip note above afterward).

**How do I know the setup worked?** Back on the `RUN` screen, the top of the display keeps showing `H…(hue) A…(area) X… Y… M…(motion)`. These are exactly the numbers the example programs read, so look at the screen first and then put those numbers in your program; that is the most accurate way.

## Values used on this page

| Name | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Hue** (color) | -1, 0 to 100 | Red 0 (100 is red too), yellow about 17, green about 33, cyan about 50, blue about 67, magenta about 83. **-1 = black, white, gray (no color)** |
| **Blob X** | 0 to 98 | Left/right position of the blob in the picture: **left 0, right 98, center about 50** |
| **Blob Y** | 1 to 75 | Up/down position: **small at the bottom, large at the top** (bottom 1, top 75), middle about 37 |
| **Blob area** | 0 to 100 | How big the blob is. **0 = no blob found** |
| **Blob width** | 0 to 98 | How wide the blob is. **0 = no blob found** (the MBC Blocks website and Pybricks use this to check) |
| **Motion value** | 0 to 100 | How much the whole picture changed compared with the previous frame; the number goes up when something moves |

> [!TIP]
> - **If you skipped "Setup 1: COLOR", hue is always 0, which is the same as red!** The program thinks it sees red when really nothing has been set up yet.
> - When no blob is found, X and Y are both 0, which looks like "bottom-left corner". So always **check whether a blob was found first** (is area or width 0?) before you look at X.

In the official LEGO App the Sharpshooter shows up as a "Color Sensor", so you read it with the Color Sensor blocks:

| Official block | What you get |
|---|---|
| **color** | Hue (-1, 0 to 100); compare it as a number |
| **reflected light** | Motion value (0 to 100) |
| **raw red** (under "More Sensors") | Blob X |
| **raw green** | Blob Y |
| **raw blue** | Blob area (0 = not found) |

> [!CAUTION]
> In the official App, **do not use the "color is [red]?" block where you pick a color**; it compares against LEGO's own color codes, not the Sharpshooter hue. Always put "color" into a variable and compare the numbers.

The data read by the MBC Blocks website and Pybricks (the "Sharpshooter school edition" blocks on the Blocks website, `MBC_cam_school_Lib.py` in Pybricks) adds **saturation, brightness, blob width and blob height** on top of what the official App gets, but has **no area**, so "blob width > 0" is used as "found" instead.

## Example 1: What color do you see?

**What this example does**: The hub display keeps showing the "hue" number the Sharpshooter sees. Put bricks of different colors at the spot you chose in "Setup 1" and the number changes.

**What you need**
- 1 SPIKE hub
- 1 Sharpshooter (with "Setup 1: COLOR" done)
- One red, one green, one blue and one white brick

**How to connect**: Sharpshooter on **port C**.

**Download the program**

| Official LEGO App | MBC Blocks website | Pybricks |
|---|---|---|
| [ex01_show_hue.llsp3](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/official/ex01_show_hue.llsp3) | [ex01_show_hue.abp](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/mbcblocks/ex01_show_hue.abp) | [ex01_show_hue.py](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/pybricks/ex01_show_hue.py) + [library](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/pybricks/MBC_cam_school_Lib.py) |

![Example 1 official App blocks](/images/sensors/esp32cam/spike-beginner/ex01-official.webp)

</details>

<details>
<summary>🟦 MBC Blocks website blocks</summary>

![Example 1 MBC Blocks website blocks](/images/sensors/esp32cam/spike-beginner/ex01-mbcblocks.webp)

<details>
<summary>🐍 Pybricks code</summary>

```python
# 神攝手（學校版）範例 1：看到什麼顏色（主機螢幕顯示色相）
# 接線：神攝手 → C 埠
from pybricks.hubs import PrimeHub
from pybricks.parameters import Port
from pybricks.tools import wait
from MBC_cam_school_Lib import MBC_CAM_SCHOOL

hub = PrimeHub()
cam = MBC_CAM_SCHOOL(Port.C)      # 神攝手插在 C 孔

while True:
    hue = cam.hue()               # 色相：0~100（紅 0／100、綠約 33、藍約 67）；-1 = 黑白灰
    print(hue)                    # 電腦畫面印出來（比較快看到）
    hub.display.text(str(hue))    # 主機螢幕一個字一個字顯示
    wait(500)                     # 等 0.5 秒再讀下一次
```

</details>

**Step by step through the program**
1. **Repeat forever**: the blocks inside keep running until you press stop.
2. **Read the hue**: the official App uses the "color" block and puts it into the variable "hue" (a variable = a box with a name that holds one number); the MBC Blocks website uses "Sharpshooter school edition C hue"; Pybricks uses `cam.hue()`.
3. **Show it on the display**: the number scrolls across one character at a time. The MBC Blocks website and Pybricks also print it on the computer screen, which is quicker to read.
4. **Wait 0.5 seconds** before reading again.

**What you should see**
- Red brick: about **0 to 5** or **95 to 100**.
- Green brick: about **30**; blue brick: about **65** (the lighting is different in every room, so the numbers vary a little).
- White paper, black brick: **-1** (no color).

**Common problems**
- **It reads 0 no matter what I put there?** → "Setup 1: COLOR" has not been done yet.
- **The number keeps jumping around?** → Classroom lights flicker, and pale colors jump the most; use a brighter, more saturated brick, or move it closer.
- **The number changed after moving to another room?** → Different lighting; do "Setup 1" again.

## Example 2: Beep when you see red

**What this example does**: When the Sharpshooter sees red, the light in the middle of the hub turns **red** and the hub beeps; for any other color the light turns off.

**What you need**: Same as example 1.

**How to connect**: Sharpshooter on **port C**.

**Download the program**

| Official LEGO App | MBC Blocks website | Pybricks |
|---|---|---|
| [ex02_red_beep.llsp3](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/official/ex02_red_beep.llsp3) | [ex02_red_beep.abp](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/mbcblocks/ex02_red_beep.abp) | [ex02_red_beep.py](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/pybricks/ex02_red_beep.py) + [library](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/pybricks/MBC_cam_school_Lib.py) |

<summary>🟨 Official LEGO App blocks</summary>

![Example 2 official App blocks](/images/sensors/esp32cam/spike-beginner/ex02-official.webp)

</details>

<details>

![Example 2 MBC Blocks website blocks](/images/sensors/esp32cam/spike-beginner/ex02-mbcblocks.webp)

<summary>🐍 Pybricks code</summary>

```python
# 神攝手（學校版）範例 2：看到紅色就亮紅燈、嗶一聲
# 接線：神攝手 → C 埠
from pybricks.hubs import PrimeHub
from pybricks.parameters import Color, Port
from pybricks.tools import wait
from MBC_cam_school_Lib import MBC_CAM_SCHOOL

hub = PrimeHub()
cam = MBC_CAM_SCHOOL(Port.C)

while True:
    hue = cam.hue()
    if 0 <= hue <= 5 or hue >= 95:    # 紅色在色相的兩端：0 附近和 100 附近都是紅
        hub.light.on(Color.RED)
        hub.speaker.beep(880, 100)    # 頻率 880 Hz，響 0.1 秒
    else:                             # 其他顏色，或 -1（黑白灰）
        hub.light.off()
    wait(100)
```

</details>

**Step by step through the program**
1. **Read the hue** into a variable.
2. **If hue is between 0 and 5, or hue ≥ 95** (the official App writes it as "> 94", same meaning) → red light, beep. Red sits at both the start and the end of the hue scale, so you have to check both ends.
3. **Else** (any other color, or -1 for no color) → light off.
4. **Wait 0.1 seconds** and check again.

**What you should see**: Put the red brick at the setup spot → red light + continuous beeping; swap in green or white paper → light off, no sound.

**Common problems**
- **It beeps all the time even with nothing there?** → Hue is 0, which means "Setup 1: COLOR" has not been done (hue is 0 before setup, same as red).
- **Orange beeps too?** → Orange hue is very close to red (about 4 to 10); make the "5" smaller, for example 3.
- **My red brick reads 7 and does not beep?** → Use example 1 to see what your red reads, then change the "5" to that number plus a little.
- **How do I pick the light color in the official App?** → Click the color dot on the "set Power Button light to" block.

## Example 3: Which side is the blob on?

**What this example does**: The hub display uses an **arrow** to tell you where the blob is in the picture: on the left → ⬅, on the right → ➡, in the middle → ⬆, not found → ✕.

**What you need**: Same as example 1; the sensor must have "**Setup 2: TRACK**" done first.

**How to connect**: Sharpshooter on **port C**.

**Download the program**

| Official LEGO App | MBC Blocks website | Pybricks |
|---|---|---|
| [ex03_blob_arrow.llsp3](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/official/ex03_blob_arrow.llsp3) | [ex03_blob_arrow.abp](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/mbcblocks/ex03_blob_arrow.abp) | [ex03_blob_arrow.py](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/pybricks/ex03_blob_arrow.py) + [library](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/pybricks/MBC_cam_school_Lib.py) |

![Example 3 official App blocks](/images/sensors/esp32cam/spike-beginner/ex03-official.webp)

</details>

<details>

<details>
<summary>🐍 Pybricks code</summary>

```python
# 神攝手（學校版）範例 3：色塊在哪一邊（主機螢幕顯示箭頭）
# 接線：神攝手 → C 埠
from pybricks.hubs import PrimeHub
from pybricks.parameters import Icon, Port
from pybricks.tools import wait
from MBC_cam_school_Lib import MBC_CAM_SCHOOL

hub = PrimeHub()
cam = MBC_CAM_SCHOOL(Port.C)

while True:
    x = cam.blob_x()                      # 色塊 X：左 0 ~ 右 98，中間約 50
    if not cam.found():                   # 沒找到色塊（這時 X 是 0，不能拿來判斷）
        hub.display.icon(Icon.FALSE)      # 顯示 ✕
    elif x < 35:
        hub.display.icon(Icon.ARROW_LEFT)
    elif x > 65:
        hub.display.icon(Icon.ARROW_RIGHT)
    else:                                 # 35 ~ 65 都算中間
        hub.display.icon(Icon.ARROW_UP)
    wait(100)
```

</details>

**Step by step through the program**
1. Read **blob X**, then read "was it found": the official App checks "is raw blue (area) 0"; the MBC Blocks website checks "blob width = 0"; Pybricks uses `cam.found()`.
2. **If not found** → show ✕ (X is 0 at this point and cannot be used for the decision, so this check comes first).
3. **Else, if X < 35** → left arrow.
4. **Else, if X > 65** → right arrow.
5. **Otherwise** (35 to 65) → up arrow, meaning it is in the middle.

**What you should see**: Hold the colored block in front of the lens and move it slowly from left to right; the arrow goes ⬅ → ⬆ → ➡. Take the block away and it becomes ✕.

**Common problems**
- **Left and right arrows are swapped?** → The camera is mounted the opposite way from the picture. In the camera menu toggle `H-Mirror` once (then check `V-Flip`, see the warning above).
- **An arrow shows even when the blob is gone?** → Something of the same color in the background is being tracked: go back to "Setup 2", lower `TOL_HUE` and raise `MIN AREA`.
- **Why is the middle 35 to 65 and not just 50?** → Leaving a band that "counts as the middle" keeps the arrow from flickering.

## Example 4: Turn to follow the blob

**What this example does**: The robot turns in place to keep the blob in the center of the camera picture. Blob on the left → turn left; on the right → turn right; lined up (or nothing in view) → stop.

**What you need**
- Everything from example 3, plus
- A two-wheel car (two motors as wheels) with the Sharpshooter mounted at the front, lens facing forward
- A colored block that you have done "Setup 2: TRACK" on

**How to connect**
- Sharpshooter on **port C**
- **Left wheel motor on E, right wheel motor on F**

**Download the program**

| Official LEGO App | MBC Blocks website | Pybricks |
|---|---|---|
| [ex04_turn_to_blob.llsp3](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/official/ex04_turn_to_blob.llsp3) | [ex04_turn_to_blob.abp](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/mbcblocks/ex04_turn_to_blob.abp) | [ex04_turn_to_blob.py](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/pybricks/ex04_turn_to_blob.py) + [library](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/pybricks/MBC_cam_school_Lib.py) |

<details>
<summary>🟨 Official LEGO App blocks</summary>

![Example 4 official App blocks](/images/sensors/esp32cam/spike-beginner/ex04-official.webp)

</details>

<details>
<summary>🟦 MBC Blocks website blocks</summary>

![Example 4 MBC Blocks website blocks](/images/sensors/esp32cam/spike-beginner/ex04-mbcblocks.webp)

<summary>🐍 Pybricks code</summary>

```python
# 神攝手（學校版）範例 4：轉頭追色塊（色塊在左就往左轉、在右就往右轉、在中間就停）
# 接線：神攝手 → C 埠；左輪馬達 → E 埠；右輪馬達 → F 埠
from pybricks.parameters import Direction, Port
from pybricks.pupdevices import Motor
from pybricks.robotics import DriveBase
from pybricks.tools import wait
from MBC_cam_school_Lib import MBC_CAM_SCHOOL

cam = MBC_CAM_SCHOOL(Port.C)
left = Motor(Port.E, Direction.COUNTERCLOCKWISE)       # 左輪：反過來裝，所以設成逆時針才是往前
right = Motor(Port.F)                                  # 右輪
robot = DriveBase(left, right, wheel_diameter=56, axle_track=112)   # 輪子直徑 56 mm、兩輪距離 112 mm

while True:
    x = cam.blob_x()
    if not cam.found():           # 沒看到色塊 → 停下來
        robot.stop()
    elif x < 40:                  # 色塊在左邊 → 原地左轉（速度 0，每秒轉 60 度）
        robot.drive(0, -60)
    elif x > 60:                  # 色塊在右邊 → 原地右轉
        robot.drive(0, 60)
    else:                         # 色塊在中間 → 已經對準，停
        robot.stop()
    wait(50)
```

</details>

**Step by step through the program**
1. **Tell the hub where the wheels are**: the official App uses "set movement motors to E+F"; the MBC Blocks website and Pybricks use "drive base: left wheel E, right wheel F".
2. **Set the speed**: 20% in the official App; the other two use "60 degrees per second". Turning too fast blurs the camera picture, so turn slowly.
3. **If no blob found** → stop.
4. **Else if X < 40** (blob on the left) → **turn left in place** (official App: steer -100).
5. **Else if X > 60** (blob on the right) → **turn right in place** (official App: steer 100).
6. **Else** (40 to 60, lined up) → stop.

**What you should see**: Hold the block in front of the car and walk slowly to the left; the car turns to follow. Stop, and the car stops facing the block.

**Common problems**
- **Blob on the left but the car turns right and keeps turning away?** → Left and right are swapped: flip the sign of both turn numbers (official App: -100 and 100; the other two: -60 and 60), or toggle `H-Mirror` as described in example 3.
- **It keeps wobbling left and right?** → Turning too fast. Lower the speed in the official App (for example 15%); in the other two change 60 to 40. You can also widen the "middle" band (change 40/60 to 35/65).
- **The car turns in place in a strange way?** → The motors are mounted the opposite way from the standard LEGO car. Official App: mount the motors the way the LEGO "standard driving base" does; MBC Blocks website: in the "drive base" block switch the "forward" direction of both wheels to the other option; Pybricks: change the left wheel to `Direction.CLOCKWISE` and the right wheel to `Motor(Port.F, Direction.COUNTERCLOCKWISE)`.

## Example 5: Motion-detection alarm

**What this example does**: Use the hub as a "security guard" that stays still. When something moves in front of the camera (someone walks past, a hand waves), the hub turns on the **red light**, beeps, and shows on the display **how many times** it has happened; when nothing moves, the light is **green**.

**What you need**: SPIKE hub, Sharpshooter (**no** color setup needed for this example).

**How to connect**: Sharpshooter on **port C**, camera pointed at a doorway or a desk, **the whole thing sitting still and steady**.

**Download the program**

| Official LEGO App | MBC Blocks website | Pybricks |
|---|---|---|
| [ex05_motion_alarm.llsp3](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/official/ex05_motion_alarm.llsp3) | [ex05_motion_alarm.abp](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/mbcblocks/ex05_motion_alarm.abp) | [ex05_motion_alarm.py](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/pybricks/ex05_motion_alarm.py) + [library](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/pybricks/MBC_cam_school_Lib.py) |

<details>
<summary>🐍 Pybricks code</summary>

```python
# 神攝手（學校版）範例 5：動態偵測警報（有東西在鏡頭前動，就亮紅燈、嗶一聲、記一次）
# 接線：神攝手 → C 埠。機器人要放著不動！
from pybricks.hubs import PrimeHub
from pybricks.parameters import Color, Port
from pybricks.tools import wait
from MBC_cam_school_Lib import MBC_CAM_SCHOOL

hub = PrimeHub()
cam = MBC_CAM_SCHOOL(Port.C)
count = 0                             # 警報響了幾次

while True:
    if cam.motion() > 20:             # 動態值：畫面變化越大數字越大（0~100）
        hub.light.on(Color.RED)
        hub.speaker.beep(880, 200)
        count = count + 1
        hub.display.number(count)     # 螢幕顯示第幾次
        print(count)
        wait(1000)                    # 等 1 秒，同一個動作不要重複算
    else:
        hub.light.on(Color.GREEN)     # 沒動靜：綠燈
    wait(100)
```

</details>

**Step by step through the program**
1. **Set "count" to 0 at the start** (a variable that remembers how many times the alarm has gone off).
2. **Read the motion value**: the official App uses "reflected light"; the MBC Blocks website uses "Sharpshooter school edition C motion value"; Pybricks uses `cam.motion()`.
3. **If motion value > 20** → red light, beep, add 1 to count, show count on the display, then **wait 1 second** (so one movement is not counted several times).
4. **Else** → green light.
5. **Wait 0.1 seconds** and check again.

**What you should see**: Wave a hand in front of the camera → red light + beep + display shows 1; wave again → 2… Keep your hands still and the light stays green.

**Common problems**
- **It keeps going off with nobody moving?** → "20" is too small. First print `cam.motion()` in Pybricks, or watch the `M` number on the sensor screen, to see what it reads when nothing is moving, then set the threshold a bit above that. Flickering classroom lights and trees moving outside the window both push the number up.
- **Waving does nothing?** → The threshold is too high; make it smaller (for example 10), or move your hand closer to the lens.
- **Can I put it on a moving car?** → No. When the car itself is moving, the whole picture keeps changing and the motion value stays high. The motion value is **only meaningful when the robot is standing still**.

---

## Example 6 (advanced): Blob area: stop when close

> [!NOTE]
> **This example is Pybricks only.** The "blob area" it uses is a number only available in sensor firmware from 2026-10 onward (two extra bytes in mode 9); the blocks in the official LEGO App and the current blocks on the MBC Blocks website cannot read it. The code itself is the example, so there are no screenshots.

**What this example does**: The robot drives toward a blob of the color you set up; the blob gets **bigger in the picture the closer it is**. Once the area reaches **1500** or more, the car stops and shows a green light. No blob in view → stop, red light; still driving → yellow light, and if the blob drifts left or right the car corrects its direction on the way.

**What you need**: Same as example 4 (the car plus a colored brick or box).

**How to connect**: Sharpshooter on **port C**, mounted at the front of the car; **left wheel motor on E, right wheel motor on F**. First set the 2:TRACK color on the sensor as described in "Before you start".

**Download the program**

| Pybricks |
|---|
| [ex06_area_stop.py](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/pybricks/ex06_area_stop.py) + [library](/examples/esp32cam/spike_beginner/pybricks/MBC_cam_school_Lib.py) |

<details>
<summary>🐍 Pybricks code</summary>

```python
# 神攝手（學校版）範例 6（進階）：色塊面積：往色塊開過去，色塊在畫面裡變得夠大（夠近）就停
# 接線：神攝手 → C 埠（裝在車頭）；左輪馬達 → E 埠；右輪馬達 → F 埠。先在感應器上設定 2:TRACK 的顏色
# 只有 Pybricks 版：面積是感應器韌體 2026-10 以後才有的數字，官方 App 和積木網站的積木讀不到
from pybricks.hubs import PrimeHub
from pybricks.parameters import Color, Direction, Port
from pybricks.tools import wait
from MBC_cam_school_Lib import MBC_CAM_SCHOOL
from pybricks.pupdevices import Motor
from pybricks.robotics import DriveBase

hub = PrimeHub()
cam = MBC_CAM_SCHOOL(Port.C)
left = Motor(Port.E, Direction.COUNTERCLOCKWISE)
right = Motor(Port.F)
robot = DriveBase(left, right, wheel_diameter=56, axle_track=112)

while True:
    area = cam.area()                 # 色塊面積 = 寬 × 高（0~7500）；沒找到是 0。越近越大
    x = cam.blob_x()                  # 色塊左右位置 0~98，50 = 中間
    if area == 0:                     # 沒看到色塊 → 停
        robot.stop()
        hub.light.on(Color.RED)
    elif area >= 1500:                # 夠大了 = 夠近了 → 停、綠燈
        robot.stop()
        hub.light.on(Color.GREEN)
    else:                             # 還小 = 還遠 → 往色塊開過去，偏左偏右順便修正
        robot.drive(80, (x - 50) * 2)
        hub.light.on(Color.YELLOW)
    print('面積', area, ' X', x)
    wait(50)
```

</details>

**Step by step through the program**
1. `cam.area()`: blob area = width × height (0 to 7500), 0 when nothing is found. It reads mode 9, the same as X and Y in examples 3 and 4, so no mode switch is needed.
2. **If area = 0** → nothing in view → stop, red light.
3. **Else, if area ≥ 1500** → close enough → stop, green light.
4. **Otherwise** → drive forward (80 mm per second) with steering = (X − 50) × 2, so the car steers toward whichever side the blob is on (same idea as example 4).
5. The library also has `cam.blob_xya()` (gets [X, Y, area] in one call, reading mode 6) plus `cam.device_id()` and `cam.firmware_version()`.

**What you should see**: Put a red brick 50 cm away: yellow light, the car drives toward the brick; the area grows as it gets closer, and it stops at roughly 15 cm with a green light. Take the brick away: red light.

**Common problems**
- **It stops while still far away / only stops after bumping into it?** → "1500" depends on the size of your brick: print `cam.area()` in Pybricks, read the area at the distance where you want it to stop, and use that number.
- **Area is always 0 but example 3 can see X?** → The sensor firmware is too old (before 2026-10) and has no area; please update the firmware. On old firmware you can compute "width × height" yourself for now: `cam.blob_w() * cam.blob_h()`.
- **Left/right correction is backwards?** → The motors are mounted the wrong way around; swap them as described in the example 4 common problems.

---

## Things to watch out for (read this first)

- **The picture freezes and the values stop updating while you are in the menu**: do not press the sensor's side button while a program is running; finish the setup, return to `RUN`, then run the program.
- **If the hub is disconnected for more than 3 seconds, the sensor picture freezes** while it waits to reconnect. That is normal; just run the program again.
- **Black, white and gray are all -1**: the current firmware cannot tell black from white.
- **Still being verified on real hardware**:
  - The current firmware (2026-10 version) was just rebuilt with updated development tools. The number ranges above were compiled from the source code and **have not yet been measured one by one on the new firmware**; if your readings differ, please tell us.
  - The MBC Blocks website and Pybricks use "blob width > 0" to decide whether a blob was found because those two have no area reading; we assume "found but width is 0" almost never happens, but this has not been confirmed on hardware.
  - The threshold of 20 in example 5 and the red range 0 to 5 / 95 to 100 in example 2 are suggested values estimated from the source code; measure with example 1 on your own field and adjust.

## Next steps

- For more precise blob tracking, change example 4 to "turn by as much as it is off": steering = (X − 50) × some number (like P control in line following).
